Two of them are acceptance criteria that rest entirely on docs/internal/skill-body-load-delivery.md, which this PR does not touch; the third is a diff-added comment in lib/test/run.sh whose universal claim is false against HEAD.

diff_profile.announcement: Diff classification: engine_self_modifying (overrides other flags' checklist) -> running full checklist. Phase 3 roster gated by Phase 3.1 applicability (has_new_types / test-relevance predicate) on every profile.

failures.claim: AC7 — docs/internal/skill-body-load-delivery.md's unestablished-reason list names the six arms the code can take
failures.evidence: The doc is untouched by this PR. Its enumeration (around line 526) still names four causes: no Skill tool_use recorded, load returned an error, no following body record, execution file unreadable/wrong shape. It omits the no-paired-result arm, the controls-unreadable arm, and the multiple-match ambiguity cause this PR introduces.

failures.claim: AC8 — the recorded delivered-whole measurement is re-derivable from bytes committed to this repository
failures.evidence: The committed fixture makes the bytes available and the helper re-derives delivered-whole from it, but the doc never names the fixture, contains no code fence and no re-derivation section, its session-C Operand column still cites only the 7-day-retention artifact of run 32674854779, and line 313 still asserts a re-derivable set that excludes the transcript. The fixture header's claim that the doc 'states the commands' is false.

failures.claim: The run.sh comment asserting every spawn goes through sbl_run so the colour neutralisation cannot be omitted later
failures.evidence: Three python3 spawns in the same #1618/#1897 block bypass sbl_run and repeat the NO_COLOR/PYTHON_COLORS prefix themselves: sbl_build (run.sh:24912), sbl_dirs_match_both_modules (run.sh:25264) and the PY_SBL_COUPLED heredoc (run.sh:25318). phase3_findings.description: The new fixture header (lib/test/fixtures/skill-body-load-transcript.observed.json, around lines 11-17) states 'the delivery record's own re-derivation section states the commands'. docs/internal/skill-body-load-delivery.md has no such section, contains no code fence at all, and never names this fixture. The fixture exists precisely because the source artifact expires in 7 days, so its stated recovery path is unusable. Diff-added prose false against HEAD -> documented_falsehood. The Phase 4.1.5 behavior-inert prose cap was evaluated: limb one holds (no tool parses this comment for behavior; strip_leading_comments discards it), limb two holds (lib/test/** is copied by neither vendor-slice.sh nor install.sh, so no consumer outside the repository reads it), so the finding is capped at Suggestion and carries no self-contradicting-diff carve-out marker. It nonetheless drives REJECT through checklist rule 1 via VC-8.

AC7 unmet. The delivery record's unestablished-reason sentence is phrased as a complete condition but names four causes where the helper now takes six arms — omitting the no-paired-result arm, the controls-unreadable arm, and the multiple-match ambiguity this PR adds. A reader is told the new ambiguity unestablished has no home in the enumeration. The doc is untouched by this PR.

AC8 unmet as recorded. The session-C row's Operand column cites only the published transcript of run 32674854779 (7-day retention); the doc never names lib/test/fixtures/skill-body-load-transcript.observed.json, and its line 313 still asserts that only the byte columns, the frontmatter split, the disable-model-invocation fact and the two git/gh status checks are re-derivable from this checkout — now false, since the transcript bytes are committed. The bytes exist and re-derive delivered-whole; the fix is a doc edit.

The diff-added sbl_run comment asserts 'Every spawn goes through here, so the colour neutralisation above cannot be omitted by a site added later — a per-site prefix has no such enforcement.' Three spawns in the same block do not go through sbl_run and each carries its own per-site prefix, so the universal is false against HEAD. Same 4.1.5 cap analysis as the fixture header (not tool-read, not shipped) -> capped at Suggestion, but VC-13 FAIL drives REJECT through rule 1.

The changeset says 'the module docstring and the two matcher-probe.yml job comments no longer describe the Skill tool_result as the verdict operand'. The diff edits one shared section header above both probe jobs plus one inline comment inside the review-tier job only; the implement-tier twin carries no such comment. The phrasing implies one corrected comment per job.

sbl_denies fails open on a fixture-build failure: sbl_says returns 'no' when sbl_build fails and sbl_denies inverts that to 'yes', which is exactly the expected value at its sole call site (the 'twice-recorded root is not refused by the error arm' assertion). A broken retry_after_error fixture would turn that assertion green while asserting nothing. Every other helper in the block fails loudly (FIXTURE_BUILD_FAILED / NO_VERDICT / grep -c). Give the build failure its own distinguishable token in both helpers.

sbl_run centralises a blanket 2>/dev/null, so a helper crash (TypeError from a new fixture shape, an unhandled OSError) surfaces only as NO_VERDICT with the traceback discarded. Because every spawn in the block now routes through this one function, capturing stderr to a retained file instead of discarding it restores diagnostics for the whole block in one line.

The '#1618/#1897 skill-body: that reason no longer names the SKILL.md file path' negative assertion reuses the exec.jsonl built by the immediately preceding assertion instead of running its own sbl_build boundary_dir. Its only guard against vacuity is statement adjacency; any later assertion interposed that rebuilds the shared exec.jsonl leaves it green while proving nothing.

The _pairs_for_root docstring says a field-keyed read 'fails open — every real reading answers unestablished if the name ever differs'. Answering unestablished is this helper's own fail-CLOSED direction (the module docstring: 'Each is unknown, not whole'), and the run.sh null_input comment uses 'fail-closed' for exactly that outcome. The real hazard described is an unfalsifiable fixture/production divergence, not a fail-open. As written the sentence contradicts the file's own vocabulary.

dirs_match's empty-operand guard is unreachable: os.path.normpath('') returns '.', so `if not a or not b: return False` can never fire and a body record with a blank Base-directory value matches a bare `SKILL.md` root. PRE-EXISTING, not introduced here — the pre-change ordering (replace-then-normpath) has the same property, verified. Fixing it means testing emptiness before normalising. Recorded as pre-existing under Phase 4.2 rule 3's in-scope qualifier.

The never-loaded reason's cause list is now incomplete. Narrowing binding to the quoted JSON form adds a third way to reach that arm — a runner recording the Skill input as a string rather than an object — which the arm's own text ('skill not invoked, or refused before any body returned') excludes, so a transcript-format drift is reported as 'the skill was never invoked'. Widen the reason and distinguish 'no Skill tool_use at all' from 'loads recorded but none bound this name'.

A run in which every root is unestablished exits 0 and reads as a green probe job. The docstring states the principle for the empty-selection case ('an audit that audited nothing must not read as an audit that found nothing') and exits 2 there, but an unreadable transcript or a show_full_output regression yields the same nothing-measured outcome at exit 0. Either exit non-zero when no root reached a measured verdict, or state in the docstring why the two cases are resolved differently. PRE-EXISTING behaviour the diff does not change.

The delivered-whole reason asserts 'contained both the file's last non-empty line and a distinctive interior line' even when read_controls found no mid control and only the tail was checked. Unreachable against the real engine roots today, but it is a verdict reason asserting evidence that was not collected. PRE-EXISTING.

The coverage-map note says 'Both runners neutralise terminal colour', but lib/test/run.sh is the only file in the tree that spawns this helper; 'both runners' appears to mean the two heredoc spawn shapes inside it. The wording sends a maintainer looking for a second runner.

The raf_body lazy-read comment carries a hand-transcribed '39KB' figure for a file that grows with every edit (currently accurate at 39,461 bytes). Under the prevention-only comment standard the load-bearing half is the prohibition, not the measurement — drop the figure and keep 'read only for the two containment scenarios'.

sbl_dirs_match_both_modules is only ever called with a POSIX-form base dir, so the backslash-bearing string a real Windows runner records never goes through the changed line. The causal branch is already reached, so this is completeness rather than a required addition.

ADVISORY, NON-BLOCKING. Neither the issue-1897 workpad nor the PR description carries a `Verification evidence:` marker. Tier classification: local/interactive (the workpad's ## Progress section carries no prflow:checkpoint gha: row). This never raises the verdict on its own.
